task: Retire legacy template implementations from active canonical authority while preserving only Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2; leave historical sources inert for later deletion and do not alter Template #3 authoring.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: The change removes legacy template implementations from active authority surfaces that feed installation, preview, AI selection, Special Commerce inventory and distinctness. Strong behavioral proof is warranted because a false retirement could either keep legacy authority alive or accidentally remove the two accepted canonical templates; physical source deletion is deliberately deferred until active reachability is proven absent.

acceptanceCriteria: The active template resolver exposes exactly gaming.playroom@20 and gaming.loot-vault@2.
Loot Vault v1 and every other legacy template key in the former active 24-package catalog resolve to no active package.
The preview theme authority imports and registers only canonical Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2 design tokens.
AI template selection and Special Commerce inventory inherit the reduced canonical catalog without a parallel legacy list.
Template distinctness uses only canonical foreign templates and excludes same-template identity from clone comparison.
No Template #3 implementation, Visual First artifact or authoring branch content is modified by this transaction.
Historical legacy source files remain inert and available only for later evidence-guided physical deletion.
The forbidden combined /szallitas-es-fizetes route no longer exists as a public page authority.
Independent /szallitas and /fizetes public routes exist, are sitemap-visible and resolve through the active storefront Page Schema shell.
Loot Vault v2 mobile/header/footer/CTA navigation uses separate shipping and payment destinations instead of the forbidden combined route.
Legacy /oldal/szallitas and /oldal/fizetes entrypoints remain backward-compatible aliases that converge on the canonical top-level routes.
Knowledge Before Build resolves instruction-governed deleted route files through the same Atlas architecture resolver as Plan Before Code.
Knowledge infrastructure change triggers the full 49-failure replay set without weakening tombstone or domain-integrity checks.
Whole-file Next route deletion does not promote generic display text, generic implementation expressions or framework page exports into global stale-reference contracts.
Deleted route/file identity remains fail-closed: stale route literals and actual file-path consumers still block unless classified as explicit instruction/tombstone evidence.
Reference Sync blocks the real stale /szallitas-es-fizetes Contact link until it is changed.
Deleting a page does not mark unrelated identical display text or same-named exports in other modules as stale consumers.
A true cross-file export consumer importing the deleted/changed origin module remains blocking.
PO-instruction and tombstone regression references to the forbidden route/path remain recognized as evidence rather than required implementation edits.
invariants: There is one active template catalog and resolver authority; retirement does not create a second registry.
Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2 remain installable, previewable and addressable through their canonical package entrypoints.
A legacy accepted or reaccepted implementation cannot become visual authority merely because its source remains in Git.
Approved generated visual references are not deleted or replaced in this inactivation transaction.
Shared Page Schema, Runtime, commerce engines, Template Factory and VX authorities are not weakened to make retirement pass.
Shipping and payment remain separate public information authorities in every active canonical template and shared route registry.
Merchant-facing route compatibility may redirect old aliases but may not restore the forbidden combined route.
Knowledge Preflight may not treat a Git-proven, instruction-governed route tombstone as an unresolved architecture file when the canonical Atlas resolver can classify it.
Reference Sync narrowing must reduce false positives without allowing live route/file identity consumers to pass.

failureModes: The catalog shrinks but a preview or AI path directly imports legacy template authority and keeps it operational.
Loot Vault v2 is omitted while legacy Loot Vault v1 remains the resolvable package.
Tests are rewritten to accept two entries while runtime resolver still exposes legacy keys.
Distinctness loses all foreign corpus evidence instead of retaining Playroom as a canonical comparison.
Physical deletion removes an approved visual reference before reference inventory is proven.
The retirement transaction touches Template #3 and obscures whether the new production system passes its first real authoring test.
A retained Loot Vault v2 regression still asserts the pre-retirement catalog state and blocks intentional canonical v2 activation.
A previously recorded Product Owner instruction remains acknowledged but unimplemented in the actual shared route authority.
The forbidden combined route is deleted without providing canonical top-level shipping and payment replacements.
Loot Vault v2 package navigation remains internally consistent but points at a route that the shared authority has retired.
edgeCases: A stale persisted legacy page key may still request preview styling even though its template package is no longer resolvable.
Special Commerce code derives its inventory dynamically and therefore should contract automatically rather than receive a second hard-coded list.
Loot Vault v2 shares the same templateKey as v1, so version-specific resolver behavior must fail closed for v1 and succeed for v2.
Same-key Loot Vault v2 must be excluded from its own distinctness corpus while Playroom v20 remains a foreign canonical reference.
Historical /oldal/szallitas and /oldal/fizetes links need compatibility without remaining canonical navigation targets.
Deleting the combined route must be represented as an instruction-governed tombstone rather than an unexplained missing page.

alternatives.summary: Remove legacy templates from active catalog, resolver, preview and derived authority surfaces while leaving source files inert.
alternatives.reason: This directly prevents interference with future authoring while preserving historical evidence until every deletion dependency and accepted visual reference is inventoried.

alternatives.summary: Delete every legacy template source, test and media artifact in one transaction.
alternatives.reason: Direct deletion has a wider dependency blast radius and risks deleting the only surviving accepted visual reference or historical proof before those assets are classified.

alternatives.summary: Keep all legacy packages active and rely on developers to ignore them during future Template Factory work.
alternatives.reason: The active catalog feeds preview, AI, Special Commerce and distinctness, so human convention cannot prevent legacy implementations from influencing later production.

specialistReviews.finding: The active 24-package catalog is the central runtime selection surface, and derived consumers should contract by consuming the same reduced canonical authority.
specialistReviews.resolution: Preserve one catalog/resolver and remove legacy packages there rather than introducing a separate active-template registry.

specialistReviews.finding: Removing legacy packages from the catalog alone is insufficient because preview themes previously imported legacy design-token modules directly.
specialistReviews.resolution: Treat direct preview imports as an authority bypass and reduce PREVIEW_THEME_BY_TEMPLATE to Playroom v20 and canonical Loot Vault v2 tokens.

specialistReviews.finding: Legacy visually rejected implementations must not remain reference material for future clone avoidance or be mistaken for Product Owner-approved visual direction.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use only the two accepted canonical templates as the active distinctness corpus and preserve old sources only as inert history until approved reference images are inventoried.

specialistReviews.finding: The shared storefront still has a concrete page module, sitemap entry and route-registry entry for the forbidden combined shipping/payment route.
specialistReviews.resolution: Treat the combined page as a planned deletion governed by PO-INSTRUCTION-SHIPPING-PAYMENT-SEPARATE and add independent canonical route modules before removing it.

specialistReviews.finding: Knowledge Preflight and Plan Before Code disagree on deleted-route architecture because only the latter uses the shared tombstone-aware Atlas resolver.
specialistReviews.resolution: Converge both gates on the existing resolver rather than adding a deletion exception or parallel tombstone registry.

specialistReviews.finding: Whole-file route deletion currently over-approximates contract identity and turns common UI text plus framework exports into required repository-wide edits.
specialistReviews.resolution: Narrow candidate generation/classification at the existing Reference Sync runtime rather than adding exceptions or a parallel guard.

specialistReviews.finding: A lexical same-value match is insufficient to prove dependency identity for generic display text or common exported symbol names when the origin file is deleted.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use origin-sensitive semantics for deleted exports and preserve tombstone evidence rather than mutating unrelated same-name consumers.

challenge.scenario: The active catalog is reduced but a legacy key can still be resolved by a hidden secondary resolver.
challenge.finding: That would make the inactivation cosmetic and violate single-authority semantics.
challenge.resolution: Regression-test explicit legacy keys against getStorefrontTemplatePackage and require undefined for every retired key.

challenge.scenario: The preview UI retains legacy design-token imports independently of package resolution.
challenge.finding: A retired template could continue influencing presentation and future visual work through a bypass.
challenge.resolution: Remove legacy preview imports and map only canonical Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2 themes.

challenge.scenario: Loot Vault v1 remains active because its templateKey matches canonical Loot Vault v2.
challenge.finding: Key-only reasoning could hide a version-authority collision.
challenge.resolution: Make v2 the sole catalog entry and explicitly prove v1 is unresolved while v2 resolves.

challenge.scenario: Distinctness loses its foreign comparison set after legacy templates are removed.
challenge.finding: An empty corpus would create a false or blocked anti-clone result.
challenge.resolution: Retain Playroom v20 as the canonical foreign corpus for Loot Vault v2 and assert corpusSize equals one.

challenge.scenario: Special Commerce or AI receives a hand-maintained replacement list that later drifts from the catalog.
challenge.finding: A second list would recreate the duplicate-authority problem retirement is intended to remove.
challenge.resolution: Leave those consumers catalog-derived and prove their inventory contracts follow the canonical catalog count.

challenge.scenario: Physical deletion is performed before accepted generated visual references are separated from legacy implementation media.
challenge.finding: That could destroy the only trustworthy visual authority for future rebuilds.
challenge.resolution: Defer physical deletion; first prove runtime inactivation, then inventory and preserve PO-approved reference images in a separate transaction.

challenge.scenario: A historical Loot Vault v2 test still requires v2 to remain outside the production resolver while the new Product Owner instruction explicitly promotes v2 to canonical active authority.
challenge.finding: Leaving the assertion unchanged would make the proof suite enforce a superseded lifecycle boundary and prevent the requested retirement state.
challenge.resolution: Update only the lifecycle expectation: v2 must resolve canonically and v1 must fail closed; retain all Factory readiness, media and Page Schema assertions unchanged.

challenge.scenario: The retirement touches a Loot Vault v2 regression governed by an active Product Owner instruction that requires separate shipping and payment public routes.
challenge.finding: Repository reality still exposes /szallitas-es-fizetes in the shared route registry, sitemap, live page and Loot Vault v2 package, so acknowledgment without remediation would preserve a known authority conflict.
challenge.resolution: Expand the transaction before further code edits: tombstone the forbidden combined route, add /szallitas and /fizetes authorities, converge legacy aliases, update the shared registry/sitemap and repair Loot Vault v2 navigation.

challenge.scenario: A Product Owner-governed route deletion is correctly represented as an Atlas tombstone, but Knowledge Before Build classifies only live Atlas nodes and therefore flags the deleted route as domain-unresolved.
challenge.finding: This creates a false BLOCK before Plan Before Code even though the canonical Atlas resolver can derive DOMAIN-STOREFRONT and shared-storefront authority for the tombstone.
challenge.resolution: Reuse the existing tombstone-aware resolveAtlasArchitectureForPath path in Knowledge Preflight for direct domain and unresolved-file evaluation; add a regression that pins this integration.

challenge.scenario: Deleting a Next.js route page causes Reference Sync to treat every removed display string, generic page export and incidental implementation expression as a repository-wide contract.
challenge.finding: The current guard emits false stale-consumer blocks for unrelated generateMetadata exports and ordinary copy such as 'Rendelési folyamat', obscuring the real route/file identity consumers.
challenge.resolution: Keep fail-closed checks for route/file/asset/component/config/data identity, but suppress generic display-text, implementation-expression and framework page-export candidates originating from a fully deleted Next route file. Preserve evidence-aware treatment for PO-instruction and tombstone regression fixtures.

challenge.scenario: Reference Sync treats all text and exported symbol names removed with a deleted page as repository-wide identities, producing unrelated stale consumers such as other pages' generateMetadata exports and generic 'Szállítás és fizetés' copy.
challenge.finding: The guard correctly found one real stale route in the Contact page, but 100+ additional findings are identity collisions rather than dependencies. Accepting them would force unrelated files into Implementation Sync and make safe route deletion practically impossible.
challenge.resolution: Preserve exact route/path/asset/component identities fail-closed, suppress ordinary display-text and implementation-expression candidates originating only from full-file deletion, scope export-symbol consumers to imports of the originating module, and classify explicit tombstone/forbidden-route test and PO-instruction references as evidence. Fix the real Contact route consumer separately.

proofPlan: Run targeted catalog, route-integrity, Special Commerce and distinctness tests against the reduced canonical authority.
Run typecheck and production build so removed imports and canonical Loot Vault v2 design-token export are compile-proven.
Run the existing Template Factory quality path to ensure canonical Loot Vault v2 remains generator-ready with the reduced distinctness corpus.
Run Release Risk and Completion Truth on the exact branch head before lifecycle closure.
Verify the branch diff contains no Template #3 authoring files and no physical deletion of accepted visual reference assets.
Run the active Product Owner instruction state check and require zero forbidden /szallitas-es-fizetes occurrences in scoped canonical route authority.
Prove /szallitas and /fizetes route modules, sitemap entries and Loot Vault v2 navigation converge on the same shared storefront presentation authority.

requirements.requirement: Only Playroom v20 and Loot Vault v2 may remain active, resolvable template package authorities.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No retired template key or Loot Vault v1 may resolve as an active package.

requirements.requirement: Preview, derived inventory and distinctness paths must not preserve a parallel legacy template authority.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Legacy design-token modules must not remain registered in the active preview theme authority.

requirements.requirement: The retirement must leave Template #3 authoring untouched and defer physical legacy deletion until accepted visual references are inventoried.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No Template #3 authoring artifact or accepted visual reference may be deleted or modified.

requirements.requirement: Shipping and payment must be separate canonical public route authorities, with the forbidden combined route removed and active template navigation converged on /szallitas and /fizetes.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: No active shared route, sitemap entry or canonical Loot Vault v2 navigation may expose /szallitas-es-fizetes.

requirements.requirement: Knowledge Before Build must classify deleted instruction-governed routes through canonical tombstone-aware Atlas architecture instead of blocking them as unresolved live files.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A deleted /szallitas-es-fizetes route governed by the active PO instruction must not produce SQ_ATLAS_DOMAIN_SCOPE_UNRESOLVED.

requirements.requirement: Reference Sync must distinguish deleted-route identity from incidental route-page copy/framework exports so the Edit-Time Guard blocks true stale machine consumers without requiring unrelated files to change.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Deleting a Next route page must not make unrelated generateMetadata exports or ordinary duplicated display copy mandatory edits.
A real live /szallitas-es-fizetes route or deleted-file consumer must still block.

requirements.requirement: Reference Sync must distinguish real dependency identity from lexical collisions during the combined-route tombstone, while still blocking genuine stale route/path/export consumers.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Unrelated display text or same-name exports may not be promoted to required implementation edits solely because a page containing the same token was deleted.
Real stale route/path consumers and true imports from a deleted export origin must remain blocking.

notes: Clean retirement transaction restarted from the verified Brabus closure HEAD because the first exploratory retirement branch received edits before its Development Plan existed. This branch intentionally restores true Plan Before Code ordering: this plan is committed first, then the already-audited authority changes are replayed. Physical deletion is explicitly deferred. Scope expanded before editing `tests/template-factory-loot-vault-v2.test.ts` after Incremental Replay exposed one superseded lifecycle assertion; guard digest and authority scope are unchanged because the added regression file is neutral test evidence. Scope expanded after Plan Before Code surfaced PO-INSTRUCTION-SHIPPING-PAYMENT-SEPARATE. Repository audit proved the combined /szallitas-es-fizetes authority still existed in runtime, sitemap, route integrity and Loot Vault v2. The transaction now includes the instruction-governed tombstone plus canonical /szallitas and /fizetes replacements before further implementation. Knowledge Before Build exposed an existing integration gap: deleted routes were looked up only in live Atlas nodes. Scope now includes a minimal tombstone-aware Knowledge Preflight convergence using the existing Atlas resolver. Because this changes knowledge infrastructure, the expected failure set expands to the canonical full replay of 49 failures and adds DOMAIN-QUALITY authority. Edit-Time Guard exposed a proven Reference Sync overreach on whole-file Next route deletion. Plan now includes a narrow existing-runtime semantic fix plus regression coverage; full 49-failure replay and guard digest remain unchanged because this is already knowledge infrastructure. Edit-Time Guard then proved one real stale Contact route plus a reference-identity false-positive class for deleted-file display text and generic export names. Scope now includes a minimal Reference Sync semantic correction and its regression coverage; subsystem set, full 49-failure replay and guard digest remain unchanged. Plan schema normalized specialist review labels to the canonical role set; review findings and resolutions are unchanged. Duplicate challenge identifier normalized without changing evidence.
